The 17-year-old, whose body was discovered on a popular beach in the coastal state last month, was initially reported by local police to have drowned. That account has since unraveled amid a post-mortem examination that found signs of assault, according to two officials familiar with the findings who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the case.

Family members of the victim, whose name is being withheld at the request of relatives, have accused officers of failing to secure the scene, ignoring witness testimony and delaying forensic collection for more than 24 hours. "They treated it as an accident from the very first hour, and they wanted it to stay that way," a family representative said in a statement issued through a British solicitor.

The case has strained diplomatic sensitivities between London and New Delhi, with the British High Commission confirming it had "raised concerns at a senior level" and was providing consular assistance. Goa, a former Portuguese enclave known for its beaches and nightlife, draws hundreds of thousands of foreign visitors annually and has long faced scrutiny over the safety of tourists.

Three police officials in the coastal district have been suspended pending an internal inquiry, a state government spokesman confirmed on Tuesday. He declined to characterize the allegations as a cover-up, describing the suspensions as "precautionary" while a special investigation team reviews the initial handling of the case.

Critics say the episode fits a broader pattern. Rights groups have for years documented cases in which the deaths of foreign nationals in Goa were prematurely attributed to drowning or drug overdoses, only to be reclassified after pressure from families and foreign governments.

"There is an institutional reflex to protect the tourism economy and, in some cases, to protect the accused," said a Mumbai-based lawyer who has represented families in similar cases and who reviewed portions of the current file. State officials have rejected suggestions of a systemic problem, insisting the new investigation demonstrates accountability.
